c1-gen-0036: The garden was green and new when a voice spoke up. Let's read Genesis 3:1 together.
c1-gen-0037: Two people in a garden, and suddenly they felt unsure. Look closely at Genesis 3:7 with me.
c1-gen-0038: Evening came to the garden, and the LORD called out. Hear His words in Genesis 3:9.
c1-gen-0039: The fruit was in her hand, and a choice came next. Follow the story in Genesis 3:6.
c1-gen-0040: After they ate the fruit, Genesis 3:7 tells what happened next.
c1-gen-0041: Footsteps sounded in the cool of the day. Turn to Genesis 3:8 and see where Adam and his wife went.
c1-gen-0042: Sad words were spoken to Adam that day. You can find them in Genesis 3:17.
c2-gen-0001: Eden's gate faced the east, and someone stood there. Genesis 3:22 and Genesis 3:24 explain why.
c1-gen-0043: Abram packed up to leave everything he knew. Listen to what God said in Genesis 12:2.
c1-gen-0044: Picture Abram on the road out of Haran, bags packed. Genesis 12:4 holds the detail you need.
c1-gen-0045: God took Abram outside and gave him something to do. Find it in Genesis 15:5.
c1-gen-0046: Abram heard God and believed Him. Genesis 15:6 is one short verse worth reading twice.
c1-gen-0047: Abraham and Isaac had a long trip ahead. Look for the place name in Genesis 22:2.
c1-gen-0048: The LORD appeared to Abram in a new land. See how Abram answered in Genesis 12:7.
c1-gen-0049: High on the mountain, a voice came just in time. Genesis 22:11 and Genesis 22:12 say whose it was.
c2-gen-0002: Father and son climbed side by side, carrying wood. Read on through Genesis 22:8 and Genesis 22:13.
c1-gen-0050: Jacob's family was big and busy. Find what he made for Joseph in Genesis 37:3.
c1-gen-0051: Young Joseph had a story to share with his brothers. Hear it in Genesis 37:7.
c1-gen-0052: The pit was dark and empty, and Joseph was alone. Keep going with the story in Genesis 37:28.
c1-gen-0053: Joseph was far from home in Potiphar's house. Walk through Genesis 39:3 and Genesis 39:4 to learn how things went.
c1-gen-0054: Joseph was locked away in prison. Even there, Genesis 39:21 has something for us.
c1-gen-0055: Pharaoh listened closely as Joseph spoke. Genesis 41:29 and Genesis 41:30 hold the full picture.
c1-gen-0056: Joseph could not keep his secret any longer. Turn the page to Genesis 45:1 and Genesis 45:2.
c2-gen-0003: Joseph's brothers stood before him, scared of what he might do. Put Genesis 45:7 and Genesis 50:20 next to each other.
c1-mat-0027: The wilderness was dry and empty. Matthew 4:1 and Matthew 4:2 set the scene, so let's look there.
c1-mat-0028: Jesus was hungry, and the tempter came near. Read his first words in Matthew 4:3.
c1-mat-0029: The devil took Jesus up very high. Matthew 4:8 and Matthew 4:9 fill in the rest.
c1-luk-0033: Jesus had a reply ready for the tempter. You'll find it in Luke 4:4.
c1-luk-0034: The crowd in Nazareth grew loud and upset. Follow them in Luke 4:28, Luke 4:29, and Luke 4:30.
c1-jhn-0020: John stood with two friends as Jesus walked past. Hear what John said in John 1:35 and John 1:36.
c1-jhn-0021: Nathanael was surprised that Jesus knew him. John 1:48 has what Jesus said back.
c2-luk-0001: Every eye in the synagogue was on Jesus as He sat down. Read Luke 4:18, Luke 4:20, and Luke 4:21 with me.
c1-exo-0010: Aaron reached out his hand over the rivers of Egypt. What followed is written in Exodus 8:6.
c1-exo-0011: Each family had a careful choice to make. Exodus 12:5 lists what God asked for.
c1-exo-0012: Moses brought a serious warning to Pharaoh. Find the time in Exodus 11:4 and Exodus 11:5.
c1-exo-0013: Every family in Israel had a job to do that night. Exodus 12:7 and Exodus 12:22 spell it out.
c1-exo-0014: God spoke to Israel about their homes. Finish His sentence by reading Exodus 12:13.
c1-exo-0015: Families got ready for seven special days. Peek at Exodus 12:15 to see what they ate.
c1-exo-0016: Moses raised his hand, and Egypt went dark. Exodus 10:22 and Exodus 10:23 answer how long.
c2-exo-0001: Egypt was full of buzzing flies that season. Exodus 8:22, Exodus 8:23, and Exodus 11:7 belong side by side.
c1-jos-0001: Joshua had a big job and a new road ahead. Hear God's words to him in Joshua 1:9.
c1-jos-0002: God gave Joshua something to think about day and night. Find out what in Joshua 1:8.
c1-jos-0003: The Jordan River was wide, and the people waited on its bank. Joshua 3:6 has his words to the priests.
c1-jos-0004: The priests stepped into the river's edge. Watch the scene unfold in Joshua 3:15 and Joshua 3:16.
c1-jos-0005: Israel walked in a long line around Jericho. Joshua 6:4 describes what the priests had with them.
c1-jos-0006: Day after day, the soldiers made their march. Joshua 6:3 and Joshua 6:14 give the count.
c1-jos-0007: The seventh day came, and the people raised their voices. See the result in Joshua 6:20.
c2-jos-0001: Joshua stood at the river, about to lead a whole nation. Joshua 1:5 and Joshua 3:7 belong together, so read both.
c1-jos-0008: Two spies were in Jericho, and the king's men came looking. Find their hiding spot in Joshua 2:6.
c1-jos-0009: The spies were getting ready to leave Rahab's house. Their last words to her are in Joshua 2:18 and Joshua 2:21.
c1-jos-0010: Caleb had waited many years for this day. Find the city in Joshua 14:13.
c1-jos-0011: Caleb remembered a time when others were afraid. Hear his words in Joshua 14:8.
c1-jos-0012: Up in the mountains, the spies waited without a sound. Count the days in Joshua 2:16 and Joshua 2:22.
c1-jos-0013: Israel was finally settled in the land. Look back with Joshua 21:45.
c1-jos-0014: Old Joshua gathered the leaders one more time. His words are in Joshua 23:11.
c2-jos-0002: Rahab had heard stories about Israel from far away. What she came to think is in Joshua 2:9 and Joshua 2:11.
c1-jdg-0001: The Angel of the LORD sat under a big tree at Ophrah. Look around the scene in Judges 6:11.
c1-jdg-0002: Gideon was surprised by a visitor that day. Hear the visitor's greeting in Judges 6:12.
c1-jdg-0003: Gideon wanted to know God's plan for sure. His test is laid out in Judges 6:37.
c1-jdg-0004: Early in the morning, Gideon went out to check. See what he found in Judges 6:38.
c1-jdg-0005: Some men went home that day, and some stayed. Judges 7:3 gives the number.
c1-jdg-0006: Gideon's men came down to the water, one by one. Find the count in Judges 7:6.
c1-jdg-0007: Picture the night: trumpets, crashing jars, and torches. Hear the cry in Judges 7:20.
c2-jdg-0001: Gideon's army looked big and ready. Yet the LORD wanted a change, and Judges 7:2 explains it.
c1-jdg-0008: Deborah sat ready to help her people. See how Judges 4:4 describes her.
c1-jdg-0009: People came to Deborah with their problems. Judges 4:5 says where to find her.
c1-jdg-0010: Jabin's army was big and hard on Israel for many years. Judges 4:3 has the number.
c1-jdg-0011: Barak did not want to go alone. Read Deborah's reply in Judges 4:8 and Judges 4:9.
c1-jdg-0012: Deborah and Barak sang after the battle was over. Hear the last line in Judges 5:31.
c1-jdg-0013: The battle turned against Sisera that day. Watch him closely in Judges 4:15.
c1-jdg-0014: Sisera was worn out after the battle. Judges 4:17 names the tent he went to.
c2-jdg-0002: Sisera's iron chariots rolled out in rows. Compare Judges 4:13 with Judges 5:21.
c1-jdg-0015: In the town of Zorah lived a man from the family of Dan. Find his name in Judges 13:2.
c1-jdg-0016: An angel brought news of a baby boy. Judges 13:5 has a special rule for him.
c1-jdg-0017: This baby would be set apart before he was even born. The special word for it is in Judges 13:5.
c1-jdg-0018: Samson was growing up near Mahaneh Dan. Something happened there, in Judges 13:24 and Judges 13:25.
c1-jdg-0019: Silver coins were offered to Delilah. Judges 16:5 lays out what the Philistine lords were after.
c1-jdg-0020: Samson sat in a dark prison in Gaza. Judges 16:22 adds one small detail.
c1-jdg-0021: The temple was crowded with Philistines. See what Samson did in Judges 16:29.
c2-jdg-0003: Samson woke up, ready to fight like before. Judges 16:20 ends with words to read closely.
c1-rut-0001: A family from Bethlehem packed up and moved away. Ruth 1:1 explains the reason.
c1-rut-0002: On the road, Naomi said goodbye to two young women. Ruth 1:14 picks the story back up.
c1-rut-0003: Ruth spoke to Naomi with her whole heart. Hear her words in Ruth 1:16.
c1-rut-0004: Ruth and Naomi had just come to Bethlehem with very little. Ruth 2:2 shares Ruth's idea.
c1-rut-0005: Ruth stood in Boaz's field, surprised at how he treated her. Listen to Boaz in Ruth 2:11.
c1-rut-0006: At the city gate, two men made a deal. Ruth 4:7 and Ruth 4:8 describe the old custom.
c1-rut-0007: A baby boy was born, and the neighbors gathered around. His name is in Ruth 4:13 and Ruth 4:17.
c2-rut-0001: Ruth's family tree kept growing after her. Look at the end of Ruth 4:17.
c1-2sa-0001: The crown was finally David's. Find his age in 2 Samuel 5:4.
c1-2sa-0002: Israel's elders came together to make David king. Their meeting place is in 2 Samuel 5:3.
c1-2sa-0003: The ark was on its way, and crowds filled the road. See what David did in 2 Samuel 6:14.
c1-2sa-0004: David's years as king are counted with care. Read 2 Samuel 5:5 to find the city.
c1-2sa-0005: David sat in his fine cedar house and thought about the ark. Read his words in 2 Samuel 7:2.
c1-2sa-0006: Nathan brought David a message from the LORD. Listen for the length of time in 2 Samuel 7:16.
c1-2sa-0007: David wondered if anyone from Saul's family was still alive. His question is in 2 Samuel 9:1.
c2-2sa-0001: David had big plans to build something for the LORD. Nathan's message runs from 2 Samuel 7:5 to 2 Samuel 7:11.
c1-2sa-0008: David sang a sad song for Saul and Jonathan. Hear the line he repeats in 2 Samuel 1:19 and 2 Samuel 1:27.
c1-2sa-0009: David missed his friend Jonathan very much. Read what he said in 2 Samuel 1:26.
c1-2sa-0010: Absalom stood by the road, shaking hands with everyone. Spend a moment in 2 Samuel 15:6.
c1-2sa-0011: David walked away from Jerusalem with bare feet and tears. Find the hill's name in 2 Samuel 15:30.
c1-2sa-0012: News from the battle reached King David. Hear his cry in 2 Samuel 18:33.
c1-2sa-0013: David sang after his enemies were gone. Read the first line of 2 Samuel 22:2.
c1-2sa-0014: David's song is full of bold word pictures. Find this one in 2 Samuel 22:30.
c2-2sa-0002: Before the soldiers marched out, the king spoke to his captains. Put 2 Samuel 18:5 next to 2 Samuel 18:32.
c1-1ki-0001: God made young King Solomon an open offer. Read his request in 1 Kings 3:9.
c1-1ki-0002: Deep inside the temple was a special room. Its reason is written in 1 Kings 6:19.
c1-1ki-0003: A queen traveled a long way after hearing about Solomon. 1 Kings 10:1 says why she came.
c1-1ki-0004: God was pleased with what Solomon asked for. See what else He gave in 1 Kings 3:13.
c1-1ki-0005: Two mothers stood before the king, with only one baby. Hear the real mother in 1 Kings 3:26.
c1-1ki-0006: The temple went up in an unusual way. 1 Kings 6:7 describes the building site.
c1-1ki-0007: Solomon's builders worked on every corner of the temple. Count the time in 1 Kings 6:38.
c2-1ki-0001: All Israel heard how the king settled the hard case. Read 1 Kings 3:9, then jump ahead to 1 Kings 3:28.
c1-1ki-0008: Elijah stood before King Ahab with a message. 1 Kings 17:1 holds his words.
c1-1ki-0009: Elijah camped by the Brook Cherith, all alone. Find out how he got food in 1 Kings 17:6.
c1-1ki-0010: The widow shared her last little cake with Elijah. Then came 1 Kings 17:16, so let's open it.
c1-1ki-0011: Elijah carried the boy down the stairs to his mother. Her answer waits in 1 Kings 17:24.
c1-1ki-0012: Mount Carmel was crowded for Elijah's test. Hear his plan in 1 Kings 18:24.
c1-1ki-0013: Elijah's offering sat ready on the altar. Then he asked for something odd, in 1 Kings 18:33.
c1-1ki-0014: On the mountain at Horeb, Elijah waited and watched. Stay with him through 1 Kings 19:12.
c2-1ki-0002: Elijah prayed out loud while the crowd looked on. Follow the moment from 1 Kings 18:37 to 1 Kings 18:39.
c1-mrk-0015: The people in Capernaum couldn't stop talking. Hear them in Mark 1:27.
c1-mrk-0016: Simon's mother-in-law was sick in bed with a fever. Jesus came in, and Mark 1:31 picks up from there.
c1-mrk-0017: A sick man came close and asked Jesus for help. Mark 1:41 is where the answer from Jesus waits.
c1-mrk-0018: Folks hurried from the town to see this man for themselves. Mark 5:15 describes him.
c1-mrk-0019: A mother came to Jesus for her little girl. Hear her clever reply in Mark 7:28.
c1-mrk-0020: Jesus looked up and spoke one special word. Mark 7:34 gives its meaning.
c1-mrk-0021: The man's first reply is in Mark 8:24.
c2-mrk-0001: Jairus was waiting, and then hard news arrived. Mark 5:34 and Mark 5:36 carry the words of Jesus.
c1-psa-0009: Psalm 13 begins with a person feeling far from God. Hear his question in Psalm 13:1.
c1-psa-0010: Psalm 27 starts like a brave song. The opening line is Psalm 27:1, so start there.
c1-psa-0011: Picture a hot, dry day and a thirsty animal. Psalm 42:1 paints the picture.
c1-psa-0012: Psalm 27 ends with words said twice. Find them in Psalm 27:14.
c1-psa-0013: Psalm 34 is a song for every kind of day. Open to Psalm 34:18 and see it.
c1-psa-0014: The writer of Psalm 56 had cried many times. Notice his request in Psalm 56:8.
c1-psa-0015: Psalm 62 asks us to trust God at all times. Read to the very end of Psalm 62:8.
c2-psa-0001: One line comes back three times in these two psalms. Spot it in Psalm 42:5, Psalm 42:11, and Psalm 43:5.
c1-pro-0009: Proverbs often puts two ideas next to each other. Read both halves of Proverbs 10:12.
c1-pro-0010: Some people talk and talk without stopping. Proverbs 10:19 has advice about that.
c1-pro-0011: Worry can feel heavy inside. Proverbs 12:25 has something to say about it.
c1-pro-0012: Two kinds of people are compared in Proverbs 11:13. Pay attention to the first one.
c1-pro-0013: Think of a leader asking friends for help. Proverbs 11:14 is the verse for this one.
c1-pro-0014: Words can sting, or they can do something else. Finish the thought in Proverbs 12:18.
c1-pro-0015: Honest words and lying words meet in Proverbs 12:22. Read it with me.
c2-pro-0001: Friends make a big difference in our lives. Proverbs 12:26 and Proverbs 13:20 are worth reading one after the other.
c1-est-0001: The king's party was loud and full of guests. Esther 1:12 shares Queen Vashti's response.
c1-est-0002: Esther was brought to the palace with many young women. See what the king did in Esther 2:17.
c1-est-0003: Esther stepped into the king's court without being called. Watch the king's response in Esther 5:2.
c1-est-0004: Everyone at the king's gate had an order about Haman. Esther 3:2 and Esther 3:5 show what Mordecai did.
c1-est-0005: Mordecai sent Esther a message with a big question in it. You can read it in Esther 4:14.
c1-est-0006: Esther was about to do something very brave. Esther 4:16 holds what she said.
c1-est-0007: Haman's plan came to light at Esther's banquet. Esther 7:10 finishes that part of the story.
c2-est-0001: First there were tears across the land. Esther 4:3 and Esther 9:22 trace that whole month.
c1-mat-0030: Jesus met with His followers on a mountain in Galilee. His words fill Matthew 28:18 and Matthew 28:19.
c1-act-0025: A chariot rolled along a desert road. Ride along with the man inside in Acts 8:28.
c1-act-0026: Philip and the Ethiopian talked as they rode. Then a question came up in Acts 8:36.
c1-act-0027: The chariot came to a stop on the road. Follow the two men in Acts 8:38.
c1-act-0028: It was the middle of the night at the jail. Begin with Acts 16:33 and look at the jailer.
c1-rom-0009: Paul writes about being raised with Christ. Stay with Romans 6:4 to its very end.
c1-gal-0001: Galatians 3:27 is a short verse about baptism. Read it once, then once more.
c2-act-0002: Two different men, two different roads, one shared moment. Lay Acts 8:39 beside Acts 16:34.
c1-1co-0001: Paul pictures the church as one body with many parts. Meet the eye and the hand in 1 Corinthians 12:21.
c1-1co-0002: God gives His people all kinds of gifts. Look for what ties them together in 1 Corinthians 12:4.
c1-1co-0003: Paul ends chapter 12 by pointing ahead. Read 1 Corinthians 12:31.
c1-1co-0004: Imagine speaking every language on earth and beyond. Paul paints a picture of that in 1 Corinthians 13:1.
c1-1co-0005: Paul names things that will one day pass away. Read 1 Corinthians 13:8 for the contrast.
c1-1co-0006: Paul wrote down the heart of what he taught. Find the day in 1 Corinthians 15:3 and 1 Corinthians 15:4.
c1-1co-0007: Many people saw the risen Christ. Check who comes first in 1 Corinthians 15:5.
c2-1co-0001: Think of a body where every part matters. Paul fills that in with 1 Corinthians 12:25 and 1 Corinthians 12:26.
c1-gal-0002: Paul speaks very personally in Galatians 2:20. Take it in word by word.
c1-gal-0003: Galatians 5:22 is a list worth knowing by heart. Let's read it through.
c1-gal-0004: The list keeps going past one verse. Read on into Galatians 5:23 until the end.
c1-gal-0005: Paul gives a simple way to walk each day. Galatians 5:16 finishes his thought.
c1-gal-0006: Helping carry someone's heavy load matters. Galatians 6:2 says why.
c1-gal-0007: Doing good can get tiring sometimes. Galatians 6:9 speaks to that moment.
c1-gal-0008: Paul uses strong pictures about how people treat each other. Look at Galatians 5:15.
c2-gal-0001: Paul talks about being free, and what to do with that. Galatians 5:13 leads right into Galatians 5:14.
c1-rom-0010: Romans 5:1 opens a new chapter with a big idea. Read the whole verse with me.
c1-rom-0011: Paul writes Romans 12:1 like a heartfelt request. What is he asking for?
c1-rom-0012: Romans 12:21 is short, but it says a lot. Try reading it out loud.
c1-rom-0013: Paul warns against just copying the world around us. Romans 12:2 explains what to do instead.
c1-rom-0014: Hard times come to everyone. Follow Paul's chain of steps in Romans 5:3 and Romans 5:4.
c1-rom-0015: Romans 12:15 has two short parts. Read both and see how they fit.
c1-rom-0016: Paul talks about many members with different jobs. Romans 12:4 and Romans 12:5 finish the picture.
c2-rom-0001: Hope sits at the end of Paul's chain in Romans 5:4. Keep reading into Romans 5:5 for the reason it holds.
c1-jas-0001: Trials can come in many shapes. Read how James wants us to see them in James 1:2.
c1-jas-0002: James talks about what testing does inside us. James 1:3 puts it plainly.
c1-jas-0003: Not sure what to do? Start with James 1:5 and James 1:6.
c1-jas-0004: James 1:22 is a short warning worth remembering. Let's look at it now.
c1-jas-0005: James gives two clear steps to follow. Read what comes after them in James 4:7.
c1-jas-0006: James asks a big question about faith and what we do. James 2:17 gives his view.
c1-jas-0007: James paints a picture of big ships out at sea. See it for yourself in James 3:4 and James 3:5.
c2-jas-0001: James looks back at Abraham on the mountain with Isaac. Connect the dots with James 2:21 and James 2:22.
c1-jhn-0022: Crowds kept following Jesus, wanting more. Hear Him in John 6:35.
c1-jhn-0023: Jesus spoke to the people at the temple. What He said about Himself is in John 8:12.
c1-jhn-0024: Jesus used a picture from everyday farm life. You'll meet it in John 10:11.
c1-jhn-0025: Martha met Jesus on the road near Bethany. Listen to Him in John 11:25.
c1-jhn-0026: Jesus was at supper with His friends, talking about His Father. John 14:6 has three things to find.
c1-jhn-0027: Jesus and His friends were together late that night. John 15:1 starts a new picture.
c1-jhn-0028: John 10:11 is worth a second look. Read the end of the verse with me.
c2-jhn-0001: John 6:35 has two halves that match. Read it all the way through.
